s: A company runs a critical API on EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group spread across three Availability Zones. Peak load needs 12 instances. A solutions architect must make the design statically stable for the loss of one AZ, meaning it must keep serving peak load without depending on launching new instances during the event. Which configuration meets this requirement MOST cost-effectively?
o: Run 4 instances in each AZ (12 total) and configure target tracking scaling so that the Auto Scaling group launches replacements in the healthy AZs.
Run 6 instances in each AZ (18 total) with the Auto Scaling group minimum set to 18.
Run 12 instances in each of two AZs (24 total) and use the third AZ only for the database tier.
Run 4 instances in each AZ (12 total) and add a warm pool of stopped instances that can be started during an AZ failure.

w.y: Static stability means the surviving AZs already have enough running capacity. With three AZs, each AZ needs 12/2 = 6 instances, for 18 in total. This is cheaper than the 24 that a two-AZ design needs, which is what 'MOST cost-effectively' rewards.

o.A: After losing one AZ, the remaining 8 instances are short of peak, and replacing them depends on launches during the event.
o.B: Correct: 6 per AZ leaves 12 running after any single-AZ loss, at the lowest standing cost.
o.C: This is statically stable but uses 24 instances, more than the 18 that the three-AZ design needs.
o.D: Starting stopped instances is still a control-plane action during the event, and warm pool capacity is not guaranteed.
